_purpose: One row per source-derived count stated in prose somewhere in this repository. Each row names WHERE the claim is written (claim_file + a pattern, never a line number — line numbers drift exactly the way the prose does, IMP-0150's own citation is the proof) and HOW to recompute the true value (derive). Adding a newly discovered stale count is a NEW ROW here, never a change to scripts/verify-derived-counts.py.
_residual: Only claims registered here are checked. A number in a sentence is not distinguishable from any other number, so an unregistered prose count stays unchecked and there is no mechanical way to find one — see the module docstring in verify-derived-counts.py.
_removed_2026_08_24: Improvement review 24 removed two rows, 'handover-2026-08-21-secured-column-count' and 'improvement-review-5-secured-column-count'. Both compared a file-wide pair count against a dated claim of 39 in a document that must never be edited, and both were therefore permanently 'historical'-exempt: they could never fire and could never be actioned. They were also two further copies of the UNSCOPED derive that produced this batch's false drift (IMP-0269) — left in place, the next person to un-exempt one would be handed 67 for a claim about a 51-column profile. The documents themselves are unchanged and remain correct as dated records. IMP-0263 established why they must not be rewritten; this removal is the other half of that decision, recorded rather than silent.

claims.description: config/revitalise-grant-automation-pipeline.yml describes the DEV and TST post-deploy seed-settings steps as seeding 'the eleven rev_setting rows'. Truth is the length of dataverse.settingRows in every deployment-settings file that carries one (dev-scoring, test, prd) — those three must also agree with each other.
The Dev Summary's security-controls table asserts the coverage test's exact-count check as '(39, not 40 or more)'. Same truth as the handover claim above.

Dev Summary section 9's verification table recorded a LIVE fieldpermissions query returning 39 on 2026-08-21, which was an exact match to source that day. Repointed 2026-08-22: that figure is a dated observation and correcting it to today's number would assert a result the query never produced, so the row now checks the sentence's live half ('source is N today') and the historical half is left standing as history.

The REV Trustee role file's own header documents the non-membership control as covering N secured columns. Pattern made tilde-optional 2026-08-22: the header said '~39' and now states the exact derived figure, and a pattern that only matched the approximate form became a REGISTRY DEFECT the moment the number was corrected -- the gate objecting to its own fix. SCOPED 2026-08-24 (IMP-0269): this claim is about REV_TrusteeRestricted specifically, and the shared FieldSecurityProfiles.xml has held a second profile since 2026-08-23. The unscoped derive returned 67 -- REV_TrusteeRestricted's 51 plus REV_FinanceOnly's 16 -- and reported the correct header as drifted. Actioning that would have written 67 into the header of the file documenting this privacy control, overstating it by the 16 Finance-only columns the trustee control does not cover. The prose was right and the gate was wrong.

The Dev Summary narrates the solution's pre-existing 'not defined in customizations' pack warnings as four; the packer emits eight (one EntityRelationship, three EnvironmentVariableDefinition, three Type='10371' GenericComponent -- plus the header line itself is not a warning). Truth is derived from the captured packer output in the Dev Summary's own build transcript: the count of indented "Type='...'" lines directly under the 'Following root components are not defined in customizations:' header. Third instance of hand-maintained-count-drifts-from-source, and the first that cost a registry row instead of a script.

derive.command: awk '/Following root components are not defined in customizations:/{f=1;next} f&&/^ *Type=/{n++;next} f&&!/^ *Type=/{f=0} END{print n+0}' docs/development/revitalise-grant-automation-dev-summary.md

claims.description: agents/improvement-agent.md's retirement rule states the retired-constraint count. It previously asserted ZERO retirements against a real ten, and pointed at a 'Retired Constraints table' in constraints/README.md that has never existed -- an agent sent to find a table that is not there learns the instruction is unreliable. Truth is the number of struck-through constraint rows across the three constraint files. Anchored on the '^| ~~C-' row shape deliberately: a naive grep -c 'status: retired' returns 11, because domain-constraints.md's header sentence explains the convention without being a retired row. Verified 2026-08-24 that all 10 anchored matches also carry 'status: retired' (zero false positives in the other direction).

skills/how-to-promote-a-finding.md anti-bloat limit 3 carried the same false claim as the improvement-agent row above, in the same words -- one rule duplicated across an agent file and the skill it loads, so correcting either alone leaves the other stale. Same derivation, same anchoring rationale.

agents/improvement-agent.md's 'Where your executable output goes' section describes scripts/ by the number of verify-*.py checks it holds. It read 42 against 43 the moment improvement review 29 added four gates — a hand-typed figure drifting from source, in the same class review 29's change 17 aliased in the digest, inside the very file that carries the anti-bloat rule about not hand-typing derived counts. Registered rather than retyped, which is the only fix that holds.

The WS-B capability workstream and two consecutive improvement reviews all restated the size of logs/known-failure-modes.md from memory. IMP-0529 and IMP-0534 are the same figure typed wrongly into two successive review gate blocks; the WS-B design document stated '572 lines / 110KB at 430 entries' as current when the file was 608 lines at 539 entries, and built its recommended cutoff on the inference that no compaction existed. The digest is the one file in this repository whose SIZE is the reason anyone changes it, so its size is the last figure that should be carried in prose. Registered rather than retyped. Anchored in the generator's own docstring rather than in agents/improvement-agent.md, which improvement review 10 deferred to the WS-H/WS-F dispatch that owns that file.
